## 2. The day's additions (verified vs inferred)
Verified in code: **D9** muse-only `WriteDisabled` (common.ps1:3170; agy/codex false), `Get-EngineTreeCheck` returns `warned`+warnings with an empty Problem for muse and `failed` for agy (codex-consult.ps1:1635-1677, 4259-4264), ledger `tree_check`; **D10** kick file protocol (`Get-KickPath` 7844, `Wait-EngineProcess` kick poll 7896, `-Kick` validation/ack 1049-1097, outcome class `operator` 4810-4815, salvage on kick 4854); **D11** roster `timeout_sec` (2493-2513, 2583-2585, single run 3029-3035, `timeout_source: roster`); **D12** stall cut (7849-7908, ledger `stall` 4064-4065, continuation with the stalled wording 4408/4442); **D13** machine health (path/env `none`, locked read-modify-write with 10 s backoff, prune by until/liveness, `running[]` liveness by pid AND start time — pid reuse safe, 5037-5195; merged into `Get-EndpointHealth` with the later-`until` tie-break 4882-4891, 4982); **D15** `partialOnFailure` only when a failed run's stream holds content — an empty first-request refusal writes nothing (4855-4868), footer "the run ended: <why>" (4913-4914); **D16** estimate (ask+brief)/4, walk skip before start, explicit `-Provider` refused (3026), fork/resume fallback with `mode_fallback` and the previous reply named in the prompt (3633-3658); **D14** Language and Live-members rules plus `Write in English.` first in all six templates. harness-fixes26b has exactly 39 checks covering each claim; muse TREE covers muse-warn and agy-fail. Two non-blocking residuals (findings #1-#2): the stall cut fires on a legitimately silent long tool run, and a kick landing in the last poll tick of a just-finished turn can mark the whole run operator-failed although its usable prose is salvaged.

findings.claim: The stall cut counts only complete event lines, so a reviewer legitimately inside one long silent tool call (a build or test run that emits nothing between item.started and item.completed) is cut as 'stalled' once StallSec (default 900 s) passes without an event, and its continuation is told to finish now without the tool's result. This is exactly what D12 defines, but it makes the default unsafe for reviews whose tool calls can exceed 15 minutes.
findings.trigger: A codex member runs a single command that produces no event lines for more than 900 s while its process stays alive.

evidence.observation: the loop breaks with Reason 'stall' when no complete line has been appended for StallSec while the process lives; no distinction between a stuck stream and an in-flight tool call
the continuation prompt then says the turn 'was stopped after N s without any output' and asks the reviewer to finish now

findings.verification: Run a fake that emits item.started for a command, stays silent 1000 s, then completes: with the default StallSec the turn is cut before completion.
findings.remedy: Treat a started-but-incomplete tool item (or a live child process of the engine) as activity, or document the bound and recommend a higher stall_sec for build-heavy reviewers.

findings.claim: A kick file written in the final poll tick of a turn that exits normally is never seen by that turn; if the run then starts another turn (a format repair or denial retry), that turn's first poll sees the stale file, is killed, and the whole run's outcome is overwritten to 'failed: stopped by the operator (-Kick)' even though the main reply was usable — its text survives only in the salvaged .partial.md. This matches the operator's stop intent, but the usable classification is lost.
findings.trigger: -Kick -Member <NN> is written in the ~1 s window after the member's main turn exits successfully but before its format repair starts.

evidence.observation: the kick file is only polled while a turn runs; a file appearing after WaitForExit returns is not consumed
RunKicked forces bridgeOutcome to 'failed: stopped by the operator (-Kick)' regardless of an earlier usable reply

findings.verification: With fakes, write the kick file in the tick between a usable prose main turn and its format repair; inspect bridge_outcome and partial_reply.
findings.remedy: When the kick was not seen by the main turn, record the operator stop as a warning on a usable reply instead of overwriting the outcome, or consume a stale kick file before starting any further turn.
